title: School Notebooks 5-pack

drivers.name: Price increase
drivers.evidence: Same price in 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05: sales were 10 and 7 units (vs baseline 7.6), suggesting ~10-20% lift in sales at lower price, now inverted; price is 2.3% higher, so demand likely down ~15%.

drivers.name: Supply risk (short delivery)
drivers.evidence: Planner note indicates supply concern; past demand drops from stockouts are not captured in baseline; conservative adjustment for lost sales.

adjustment.analysis: No events or promotions are scheduled. The price increase to $9.03 (+2.3%) is likely to suppress demand, especially given recent history: the same price point in 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05 saw sales drop to 10 and 7 units, respectively, below baseline (7.6). The supplier warning of short delivery introduces supply risk, which may dampen customer intent. No noise-adjusted uplift from past promotions or holidays is credible. The classical model’s 1.00 is unadjusted for this price hike and supply risk. The median should reflect a modest downside.

brief:
PRODUCT: School Notebooks 5-pack | category Office | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-22 (6 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 9.03 (+2.3% vs regular price 8.83)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 7.6 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 37.9 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 24.5

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-64% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
